newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Montenegro's Crna Gora Sume sells shares - agency.
newsitem.headline: Montenegro's Crna Gora Sume sells shares - agency.

text.p: Montenegro's forest exploitation company Crna Gora Sume from Pljevlja has put on sale 24.39 million dinar ($4.27 million dollars) worth of shares in a public offering, state news agency Tanjug said.
Shares can be subscribed by June 10, Tanjug said on Thursday.
The value of capital of the socially-owned company is estimated at 81,303,000 dinars.
Crna Gora Sume is selling 24.391 million dinar worth of shares at a face value of 1,000 dinars with a 30 percent discount.
It will distribute 8.131 million dinars worth of shares free of charge to the workers. To qualify for free shares, workers need to have at least three years of service with the company.
Crna Gora Sume plans to transform into a shareholding company by capital increase, share issues and free distribution of shares.

The remaining unsold portion of socially-owned capital, the owner of which has not been determined, will be transferred to three Montenegrin state funds in line with the republic's privatisation law. -- Beti Bilandzic, Belgrade newsroom +38111 222 4305
